clue.text: Novices cute when off on the trot

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Novices look sweet when they head off at a trot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the trot' looks like part of the riding picture, but it is the definition: British slang for in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: On the trot is a British idiom for one after another, in unbroken succession.

clue.text: Be honest — might this mean 'Down with leaders of new world order'?

parts.words: might this mean 'Down with leaders of new world order'
parts.note: the leaders of new world order are N, W, O; read as an instruction for a down light, the answer says to write those three first letters going upwards

explanation.surface: A protest slogan against a sinister new world order, recast as a call for honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading letters of 'new world order' are N, W, O; written upwards in a down light they spell the first word of the answer, followed by its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit or confess something is to be honest about it; a phrasal verb of confession.

clue.text: Horse caught prancing with Zulu — that's lively!

indicators.note: a prancing horse moves about wildly, so these letters jump into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Zulu is the NATO alphabet word for Z

explanation.surface: A horse is caught capering with a Zulu warrior, which is certainly lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a quick, playful movement in a symphony or sonata, so a lively piece of music.

clue.text: Shells from what sounds like male crab found on shelved area regularly

indicators.note: the clue says outright that a sound-alike is wanted for the male crab

parts.note: a male crab is called a cock crab

indicators.note: taking every other letter, at regular intervals, from the words shelved and area

explanation.surface: Seashells come from a male crab found on a shelving stretch of beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks the even letters of 'shelved area': H, L, E, A, E.
explanation.definitionFit: The cochlea is the spiral cavity of the inner ear, shaped like a snail shell; these are its plural.

clue.text: Nervous leader tumbling in race

indicators.note: the leading letter falls away from the word for nervous

parts.note: windy is British slang for nervous or scared

explanation.surface: A jittery front-runner takes a tumble during a race.
explanation.walkthrough: WINDY is informal British for frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indy, short for the Indianapolis 500, is a famous American motor race.

clue.text: Urge on investigations into pre-natal cover-ups?

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them on
police cases are investigations

explanation.surface: Pressing for inquiries into antenatal scandals that were hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg cases are protective coverings that shelter eggs before hatching, hence whimsical covers before birth.

clue.text: Disaster in Salt Lake City? Say no more — not to be entered without prior arrangement

definitions.text: not to be entered without prior arrangement

indicators.note: a disaster turns things upside down, so the letters are rearranged
says the letters of the word say are to be taken away from the jumble

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A catastrophe in Utah's capital, and the speaker would rather not elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S, A, Y from the letters of SALT LAKE CITY and rearrange the nine left.
explanation.definitionFit: An event that is all-ticket admits only those holding tickets bought beforehand, so no walk-ins.

clue.text: Undoubtedly, as we hear, cook suited for land jobs

indicators.note: as we hear signals that the preceding word is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: sure means certainly, undoubtedly

indicators.note: to cook the books is to fiddle them, so the letters are falsified into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef was surely fitted out to work on dry land.
explanation.walkthrough: In standard British speech SURE and SHORE sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Shore duties are a sailor's postings ashore, tasks on land rather than at sea.

clue.text: Keep close when retreating round edges of Languedoc valley

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other
retreating means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to hug is to keep close

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Huddling together while withdrawing around the borders of a French region.
explanation.walkthrough: Languedoc is a region of southern France; its name serves only for its edge letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow, steep-sided ravine, a kind of small valley in American usage.

clue.text: Given full rein, Navratilova's said to wear a French dress initially

indicators.note: wearing means being put on, so the sound-alike word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: une is French for a

indicators.note: said signals a sound-alike of the nationality

parts.note: Martina Navratilova, the tennis star, is Czech

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word dress

explanation.surface: Navratilova, given free rein, is rumoured to wear a French frock.
explanation.walkthrough: Martina Navratilova was born in Czechoslovakia; 'said' turns her nationality into the homophone. 'Dress' seems to be what she wears, but only its initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchecked means unrestrained, allowed to run free like a horse given its head.

clue.text: Mast down, search party's launched for sailor …

indicators.note: down means taken out, so the mast word's letters are removed from the pool
launched means sent off, so the remaining letters are set in a new order

parts.note: the possessive gives no letter, so the fodder is the two words as written
a spar is a pole used as a mast

explanation.surface: With the mast down, a search party sets off for a lost sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S, P, A, R from SEARCH PARTY and rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachter is a person who sails a yacht, so a sailor of a particular kind.

clue.text: … mast finally OK, Mr Dennis is animated

parts.note: a spar is a pole used as a mast

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of OK

parts.note: Les Dennis is a British TV presenter and comedian

explanation.surface: Continuing the rescue: the mast is finally fine and Les Dennis gets lively.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Dennis was the long-time host of the British TV quiz Family Fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sparkles is lively and vivacious, full of animation.

clue.text: Outdoor skills take Signal Corps seawards on carbon floats

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for Signal Corps
a tide going out flows seawards
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
rafts are floats

explanation.surface: Survival training: the Signal Corps heads out to sea on charcoal-laden rafts.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoutcraft covers the fieldcraft of Scouts: knots, tracking, camping and similar open-air abilities.

clue.text: Hawking without a bit of training can be vexing

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to hawk is to clear the throat and spit

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the first letter of training

explanation.surface: Stephen Hawking, short of some practice, can still be irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawking' suggests the physicist; here it means clearing the throat and spitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiting someone is deliberately annoying or hurting them, so vexing them on purpose.

clue.text: Kindly spend a pound (when you get it) for green container

indicators.note: spending money means giving it up, so the pound sign letter is lost

parts.note: please, as in kindly do this
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
COD, cash on delivery, means paying when you get the goods

explanation.surface: Please pay a pound on delivery for the green bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spend a pound' echoes the British euphemism 'spend a penny', meaning to visit the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasecod is an old word for a pea pod, the green case holding the peas.

clue.text: Gosh! Duke's in nothings!

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: O looks like zero, so two nothings are two Os
D is the abbreviation for duke, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that a duke is among the nonentities.
explanation.definitionFit: Odso is an archaic exclamation of surprise, an old mild oath much like heavens.

clue.text: Describing one of 'Three Ships' in carol?

indicators.note: in places the ship inside the verb

parts.note: to carol is to sing
a ketch is a two-masted sailing ship, as in the carol I Saw Three Ships

explanation.surface: Talking about one of the vessels from the Christmas carol about three ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketching means outlining or portraying briefly, so describing in broad strokes.

clue.text: Rector's put in to settle faulty scholarship

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside another
faulty suggests something wrong, so the word settle is jumbled up

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A rector is installed to sort out a flawed bursary system.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters, as in a man of letters, means learning and literary scholarship.

clue.text: Light unit reportedly being on sale is fortunate

indicators.note: reportedly signals a sound-alike of the light unit

parts.note: the lux is the SI unit of illumination
a book or record that is out is available to buy

explanation.surface: A lighting unit, said to be on sale, is a lucky find.
explanation.definitionFit: To luck out is an idiom meaning to have good fortune, to be lucky.

clue.text: Pleasurable new pub's lacking older tipples

indicators.note: new says the letters are made over into another order
lacking says the letters of the word pub are missing from the pool

parts.note: the word pub, the possessive giving no letter

explanation.surface: A pleasant new bar without the old-fashioned beers.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, U, B from PLEASURABLE and rearrange the eight left.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ales are traditional cask-conditioned beers, an older style of drink.

clue.text: A case for contributing to the Tuileries

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A justification for donating to the Paris gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Constituent of power on the Hill?

parts.note: elec is short for electricity, power
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Part of the energy supply on Capitol Hill, the seat of US political power.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a voter in a constituency, one who elects a representative.

clue.text: Whale of a time over in an EEC country, initially touring

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the others
initially takes the first letter of the word country
touring means travelling around, so these letters wander into a new order
over means turned over, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Having a whale of a time touring one of the old Common Market countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring' rearranges AN EEC plus C into CECEAN; 'over' turns A T into TA, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cetacean is any member of the order of aquatic mammals including whales, dolphins and porpoises.

clue.text: Ships lots of oil round mid-September

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around the other

parts.note: oil is measured in gallons
E is the middle letter of September

explanation.surface: Tankers carrying vast quantities of oil around the middle of September.
explanation.definitionFit: Galleons were large Spanish sailing ships of the 15th to 17th centuries.

clue.text: Some man in Japan's a killer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A certain man in Japan is a murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a feudal Japanese warrior trained in espionage and assassination.

clue.text: Difficulty expressing a concept is a setback in star with no Latin

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the trimmed star
with no means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: alpha is the brightest star in a constellation

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the two little words are read backwards

explanation.surface: Struggling to put an idea across is a blow to a would-be star without Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no' removes L from ALPHA to leave APHA; 'setback' turns IS A into ASI.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphasia is a disorder, often after a stroke, impairing the ability to use or understand language.

clue.text: Punishment for raising mobs alleviated somewhat

indicators.note: raising in a down light means the letters are read upwards, in reverse
somewhat means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A penalty for stirring up crowds was eased a little.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was an Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a British court order against nuisance behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: An ASBO was a civil penalty restricting the behaviour of someone causing public nuisance.

clue.text: With the first idle question egghead revealed point of schemata

indicators.note: the first letter is idle, out of work, so it is dropped

parts.note: to ask is to question
the head of the word egg is its first letter
to let on is to reveal
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A lazy first question reveals a brainbox's point in the diagrams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With the first idle' drops A from ASK to leave SK.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeletons are bare frameworks or outlines, which is what schemata are.

clue.text: British eccentric backing prince from Penang

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British
a nut is an eccentric person

explanation.surface: An odd British figure supporting a Malaysian prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunku is a Malay title for a prince, used in states such as Penang.

clue.text: Maybe the 'Spey' crew welcomes crush on steamer?

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a crew is a team
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A boat crew is smitten with a passion aboard a steamboat on a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spey is a Scottish river famous for salmon and trout fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spey is a river full of game fish, so an example of a fishing water; 'maybe' marks the example.
